text:
alex: Quick heads up — our nightly eval GH Actions job started failing around 03:05 PST after the matrix bump. Seeing 'No runners with label 'large-eval'' then long timeouts. Logs excerpt:

``
Run evals/nightly
Using Ubuntu-latest
Error: No runners with label 'large-eval' are online
Action timed out after 60m
Exit code 1
```

maria: Ugh, this is the GH concurrency / self-hosted runner problem again. We should either move the heavy matrix to buildkite or add a dedicated fleet for ‘large-eval’. GH is killing our parallelism.

sam: Agreed. For immediate relief: split the workflow into two jobs — a tiny “smoke-eval” that runs on github-hosted runners (PR gating) and a heavy “nightly-matrix” that runs on buildkite/self-hosted. That avoids blocking PRs.

maria: +1. Also we can gate the heavy quantization experiments to nightly only; PRs shouldn't run full quant tests.

tanya: If we add a required “smoke-eval” check, it might slow some PRs. Can the smoke be <= 30s? What subset do we run?

sam: Make smoke = 2 short scenarios: one generation (length 32) + one embedding sanity. Yields are stable and catch obvious regressions. Example GH Actions job snippet:

```yaml
name: eval-smoke
runs-on: ubuntu-latest
steps:
  - run: pip install -r requirements.txt
  - run: pytest tests/evals/smoke_tests.py -k "short"
```

devex: Also propose: make smoke check required for main branch protection but optional for draft PRs. And for metric tolerances, link to docs: https://internal.redwood.ai/docs/evals/metric-tolerances (we should update tolerances for quantized runs).

alex: Good call. One more thing: the nightly job sometimes leaves orphaned artifacts and then the artifact uploader times out. We need a retry/backoff in the artifact step.

ci-bot: CI Notice: restarted workflow 1918765432-run #47 by @maria :repeat:

maria: I'll open a quick PR to: 1) add smoke-eval GH Action, 2) change heavy matrix to buildkite trigger, 3) add exponential retries to artifact upload. Targeting EOD.

tanya: Can you also add a short note in the PR about metric definitions — floating-point tolerance changed in quantized runs caused previous CI flakiness (see internal slack thread and docs).

alex: Action items summarized: 
- migrate heavy quant/matrix to buildkite (maria)
- add eval-smoke required check (sam)
- add retry/backoff on artifact uploads (maria)
- update metric tolerance doc and add link in PR (devex/tanya)

sam: I'll draft the smoke_tests.py example and a minimal Docker action if needed.

devex: If anyone wants a template for the branch protection rule and required checks, I have one in the devex repo. Ping me. :thumbsup:

maria: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/782 (contains smoke job + buildkite trigger) — please review.

alex: Thanks everyone. If CI still flakes after this, we can throttle GH runner concurrency and route heavy shards to dedicated cluster.

ci-bot: Reminder: nightly build scheduled at `0 11 * * *` UTC (11:00 UTC = 03:00 PST).

maria: I'll follow up with a short postmortem if the change doesn't stabilize by tomorrow.
